THE PREAMBLE, verbatim:
## Slice two units

One row is one PR, from main, signed and through the merge queue after the
operator rules. Follow this order. Dependencies are semantic prerequisites,
not simply the preceding row; the independence of U1–U4 is explicit in D9.
No row through U9a lifts the MCP compile fence. U9b is the sole enabling PR.
The lettered splits are required by the checked seams: record schema plus
embedded copy already consumes two files; multi-server wiring crosses runtime,
protocol and adapter data; storage/folding/inspect crosses CLI, protocol,
runtime and pure view. Minimal ledger writing is deliberately pulled into U6.

`contracts/realms.v<N>.schema.json` denotes one exact future file allocated
as **the next realms version after v7** at U5c, including v7's fields. It is
the only intentionally deferred filename number. Every other production path
below is literal. New paths are proposed modules/schemas, not files created
by this document plan. Constructors/registration are counted in their row.
Future tests extend the named suites; capability_broker already exists under
the consolidated CLI integration binary. New capability_artifacts and runtime
capability_ledger/capability_broker_launch modules are registered through the
existing test-only roots (CLI tests/it.rs and runtime tests/it.rs), not new
undeclared binaries. Tests may use child modules of the owning suites to stay
below 2,000 lines; list every test move in unit evidence.

Each row closes exactly its numbered tasks, including tests/mutations and
gate evidence. Test lists below are the allowed owning suites; every row
also updates this change's tasks and later implementation evidence. Measured
witness/compose pins accompany only rows that change their inputs.

YOUR UNIT, verbatim:
### U7c0b — Observe a server box for provisioning, under the startup bound

Split before U7c (operator ruling 2026-10-15): U7c's second run (0065-slice-two-unit-u7c-see-the--d7c398e5) stopped blocked after review, because the engine could reach the server box observer only through `ServerBox::prepare`. That entry judges MB3's write exclusion against the observing process, its parent and its grandparent. The engine is no managed writer and none of the three is confined, so every multiply-linked or unreadable root-owned support file (an ordinary system set holds them) refused filesystem identity for every plan; and the observation ran synchronously before the attempt's deadline, with no bound and no cancellation.

In the protocol, add one public provisioning entry beside `ServerBox::prepare` that observes the same box and returns the same bounded `Sources`, judging write exclusion against the writers the plan seals (`ServerProfile.writers`, beside the kernel's overflow uid) taken as confined, as the plan seals `Privilege::Confined`, and not against the observing process chain. This changes nothing the broker proves: at admission its observer still reads the real managed writers (itself, the broker, the harness), adds the sealed ones, proves their confinement and compares with the sealed Sources and Writers, refusing filesystem identity where they are not confined. Off Linux the entry refuses as `prepare` does. namespace.rs is at its line ceiling, so the entry may live in a new private child beside it under the standing child-module rule; the credential construction lives in `crates/brokkr-protocol/src/hands/namespace/sources/host.rs`.

In the CLI, add one hidden `BrokerCmd` verb, registered in `crates/brokkr-cli/src/cli_args.rs` and dispatched in `crates/brokkr-cli/src/broker.rs`, whose arguments and body live in the new private child `crates/brokkr-cli/src/broker/survey.rs`, so cli_args.rs (at 788 of its 800 lines) takes only the enum variant. The verb reads one closed, bounded request record on standard input (the server launch, the engine's HOME, the seat's reach, the network and the sealed writers), resolves the program and hashes the bootstrap (the current Brokkr binary) itself, runs the provisioning entry, and writes one closed reply on standard output: the resolved executable and tree, the bootstrap digest and the `Sources`, or the refusal's typed cause. Both records live in `crates/brokkr-protocol/src/broker.rs` through the `records!` macro, so neither side keeps a second copy of a wire name. The verb carries no authority: it reads no store, plan or secret, and writes no file outside the box scratch that the hands `Session` makes for the generated identity, which the observation digests as admission does; the session removes it on drop and, after a kill, leaves it to the #415 reaper, exactly as `serve`'s observer does (operator ruling 2026-10-15). It is the engine's counterpart of `serve`'s observer helper (U6c5b): U7c runs it as a killable child in its own process group under the attempt's startup deadline and remaining bound, and kills and reaps the group on expiry or cancellation, so no worker survives.

The public API rises by the provisioning entry (`ServerBox::provision`), the request (`Survey`), the reply (`Provisioned`, `Surveyed`) and the closed causes of an unread request (`Unread`): brokkr-protocol's listing goes from 1136 to 1162 lines, +26, as measured at the first run (operator ruling 2026-10-15).

Closes tasks 35.1 and 35.2 with U7c0 and U7c; requirements [MB3](specs/mcp-capability-broker/spec.md), [SD4](specs/slice-two-delivery/spec.md), [SC1](specs/slice-two-contracts/spec.md).
Proof: Over a real multiply-linked support file, the provisioning entry admits under sealed confined writers where `prepare` in an unconfined process refuses identity; a sealed writer owning the file, a group or other write bit, an access ACL, an unmapped or overflow owner and an empty writer set each still refuse, exactly as at admission. The request and reply round-trip equal with their exact wire names; an oversized, truncated, duplicate-key or unknown-field request refuses; a missing program or a refused source set writes its typed cause and exits nonzero, with nothing else on standard output. Bind each with a compiling removal.

Owning tests: the protocol's hands tests (`crates/brokkr-protocol/src/hands/tests/`), the broker records' test module, and a test module beside `broker/survey.rs`.

CONTROLLER'S STATE FOR THIS RUN (the-forge-67, 2026-10-15). This is U7c0b's SECOND RUN.
- The first run (0065-slice-two-unit-u7c0b-see-th-6286d937) implemented U7c0b as 5d767d43 and passed verify. Review returned M1–M4, L1, L2 and I1.
- Its reforge, 742f8eeb, answered M1, M3, M4, L1, L2 and I1, then stopped IMPL-BLOCKED on M2 alone: the verb "writes nothing", yet `served` digests the generated identity files and the scratch mount they sit on.
- The operator ruled on 2026-10-15; see U7c0b's section in design.md as amended in your worktree:
  (a) The box scratch the hands `Session` makes for the generated identity is within the contract. It is removed on drop and, after a kill, left to the #415 reaper, exactly as `serve`'s observer leaves it. Do not redesign the observation.
  (b) The public API rise is approved as measured: brokkr-protocol 1136 → 1162 lines (+26), for `ServerBox::provision`, `Survey`, `Provisioned`, `Surveyed` and `Unread`.

YOUR WORKTREE ARRIVES WITH BOTH COMMITS' WORK STAGED. prep replayed d5dbb162..742f8eeb onto main, with the design amendment, and then wrote the two rulings into U7c0b's section. It left out quality/file-lines.txt: regenerate it. KEEP the replay. Check it against main, which has moved since d5dbb162; rerun every gate; fix only what fails or what this note names; commit signed.
- evidence/U7c0b.md: replace the scratch exception (around line 69) with the operator's ruling. State the API exactly as measured on your head: old → new, and every added line. If the number differs from +26, say so plainly; the controller takes it back to the operator.

- The review seat's validation skipped the real-host contrast; on this host it runs (205,078 entries over 2 mounts). Keep it running here, and skip it with a printed reason only where no multiply-linked system file exists.

OUT OF SCOPE: as the first run's: anything in brokkr-runtime (U7c); the broker's admission-time observation and its writer proof; sources.rs's identity observation. If something cannot be done inside the row and its existing private children, stop with IMPL-BLOCKED and name it.

GATES: as the first run's note: protocol --lib, cli --lib broker:: plus the verb's tests, cli `--test it capability_broker::`, runtime --lib, workspace clippy -D warnings, fmt, typos, openspec validate --all --strict, quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api, and llvm-cov --branch over the changed files. The controller runs the exact coverage gate and the crap ratchet on the host.

STANDING RULINGS. Decision 0065's hold: off by default, no grandfathering; realm-only grants; tools are an abstraction, dialects the concrete; refuse, never reconcile (slice one's operator ruling of 2026-09-23). The MCP compile fence stays in place until U9b. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063). Main's code-health rules bind: no `unsafe` in brokkr-runtime; `#[expect(.., reason)]`, never `#[allow]`; clippy's too_many_lines, excessive_nesting and struct_excessive_bools are denied, so split, and only if splitting would widen your unit carry `reason = "baseline 2026-09-29, decision 0065 slice one merged with main; split after #319"`; when a count moves, re-measure quality/'s file-lines, too-many-lines and suppressions (the steps quality/measure.sh uses), witness pins with `BROKKR_BLESS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test witness_digests` (or, once #423's single test binary is on your base — crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/it.rs exists — `BROKKR_BLESS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test it witness_digests::`), and budgets with scripts/measure-budgets.sh. Where a crate has tests/it.rs, a NEW tests/*.rs file must be registered as `mod <file>;` in that crate's tests/it.rs (layering::test_targets refuses an unregistered one), unless it sets HOME, cwd, env or a global allocator, in which case it is its own [[test]] in Cargo.toml with the reason written there; and `--test <file>` filters become `--test it <file>::` (capability_launch stays its own binary).

RULES. Touch at most the production files your row names; if the real scope exceeds them, STOP and report `oversized` with the split. One exception, the operator's standing rule of 2026-10-09 (operator-ruling-2026-10-03.md): beside a production file in your row that sits at its 800-line ceiling, or is frozen at its quality/file-lines.txt baseline above it, you may add NEW private child modules, declared from that file, in its own module tree and consumed in this unit, without stopping. The same holds beside a row file that your own change would push past 800 lines (extended 2026-10-11). You may also change an EXISTING private child module of a file in your row, in that file's own module tree (extended 2026-10-11). You may move existing code out of the full file into such a child to make room, preferring the code your change touches. Name each new file in your evidence and commit, and set its quality/file-lines.txt row. You may also add a name to an EXISTING re-export in the parent module that declares one of your row's files, where the parent's line count does not change (extended 2026-10-10). Files in any other module tree still mean `oversized`; any public API growth still needs the operator's ruling at PR time (record it, do not stop). Test files are NOT bounded by the row (controller's standing clarification, 2026-10-05): a test anywhere that pins behaviour your unit changes, a validator or fixture swap in another suite, or a new child test module beside an owning suite that sits over its line ceiling is part of your unit — size-neutral wherever a file sits at its quality/file-lines.txt baseline. A LOW finding you cannot fix inside your row's production files: record it in your result and do NOT report blocked for it. Tests assert exact reasons and values, never is_err(); every new test is bound by a compiling mutation that makes it fail, then restored, recorded (test, assertion) in evidence.md. Tick a task in tasks.md only on observed evidence; record results in a NEW file of your own, openspec/changes/decision-0065-capabilities-slice-two/evidence/U7c0b.md (two lanes deliver units at once, and every unit appending to evidence.md made each pair of pull requests conflict), and do not edit evidence.md itself; write it in prose or a table — never as a bullet list of the standard gate lines (`cargo fmt ...: clean`, `cargo clippy ...: clean`), which earlier evidence files already hold word for word, so the data clone gate refuses it; never edit the tasks.md preamble. Fixtures build on a canonicalised temporary root; no test reads .forge/ or needs an installed provider. Frozen contracts, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/ and extensions/ do not move unless your unit names them. Sign every commit (`git commit -S`; main requires signatures). HEADLESS SEAT: your session ends the moment you end a turn — never run a command in the background, never use Monitor or ScheduleWakeup, run every command in the foreground under the tool's 10-minute limit (suites crate by crate with `timeout 590`, split by --lib/--test if longer), and write your result file before you finish. GATES: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; the suite of each crate you touched; openspec validate --all --strict; typos --hidden; git diff --check; quality/ratchet.sh files and clones. CI also builds and tests on macOS, which this host cannot: Linux-only code (namespaces, mountinfo, /proc, device numbers, Linux-only syscalls) goes behind `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]` with a non-Linux stand-in that refuses, as broker/session.rs does, and any libc or rustix type you use must be the same type on both (rustix's Dev is u64 on Linux and i32 on macOS; U6c6a's first PR failed to compile there). Keep the session small; commit when the unit is done; never push.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

members.adversarial: Security review of the single commit 589f244e (origin/main 64027718..HEAD, U7c0b), read-only. Scope: the changed protocol files (broker.rs records, hands/namespace.rs, new namespace/provision.rs, namespace/sources/host.rs), the changed CLI files (broker.rs, broker/session.rs, new broker/survey.rs, cli_args.rs), their tests, and the docs/quality rows. I confirmed the diff adds no contracts/, fixtures/, policy/ or reference/ changes and that the commit is signed. Injection: the only new protocol edge is Survey (request) / Surveyed (reply). Survey and Provisioned are built through records!, so each is parsed through a map-only Object with deny_unknown_fields, no positional form, and one Serialize; Surveyed and Unread are closed externally tagged enums. request() reads at most 1 MiB + 1, then from_slice requires a single value with only whitespace after, so duplicate keys, unknown fields, truncation, oversized input and input errors each map to their typed Unread cause. launch goes only to ServerProgram::resolve (path lookup against a fixed SERVER_PATH, no shell, no argv interpolation); home is is_absolute() + canonicalize; reach/network/writers feed only comparisons and the bounded observer. The reply is serde-serialized, so a path with newline/JSON metacharacters cannot splice a second record onto the engine's line reader; a non-UTF-8 path fails serialization and exits nonzero with no reply (fail-closed). Secrets/journal: survey reads no store, plan or secret, writes no journal, mutates no env, and its reply carries only paths, a tree, a sha256 bootstrap digest and bounded source counts/digest, so no secret or model prose can reach the append-only journal. Fail-closed: run() writes exactly one reply and exits 1 for every Refused and every Unread, 0 only for Provisioned; tests pin all three streams. ServerBox::provision is the deliberate, operator-ruled (2026-10-15) entry: on Linux it runs the same prepare_with -> prepared -> served path with Host::provisioning(sealed), which is provisioned(overflow, sealed) = sorted/deduplicated sealed uids, parsed overflow uid and Confinement::Proved, or Credentials::unknown() (Unproved) for an empty sealed set or an unreadable overflowuid. That is a local weakening of the write-exclusion refusal, but it confers nothing: provision returns only Sources, not a box or writers, and its only production consumer is the authority-free survey. Admission is untouched and re-proves: Host::live still reads the real managed chain (self, broker, harness), and Credentials::sealed/launched/credited/excluded/untouchable are semantically identical to before (credited and Host::live are behaviour-preserving extractions; overflowed is the same parse). The broker's compared() still requires observed sources == sealed sources and set(observed union sealed) == set(sealed) with the observed confinement proved, so any file the survey admitted under assumed confinement but the real chain cannot protect is refused at admission, never admitted. I verified no other caller of provision, Host::provisioning or provisioned exists in production. Tamper paths: the sealed writers only ever make the proof stricter (owner/mode/ACL/overflow checks are unchanged); the box, handles and Session scratch are dropped inside provision before the reply, and the operator ruled the scratch in (removed on drop, #415 reaper after a kill). The bootstrap is observed as a source and mounted by handle, so content/digest tampering is caught by the sealed Sources comparison. canonical_home is a shared, behaviour-preserving extraction. No unsafe, allow/expect, shell, Debug-format-in-digest, unwrap or panic path was introduced. Residual nits are info-level only and not security: Surveyed's deny_unknown_fields is inert on an externally-tagged newtype-variant enum (the variant set is what closes it), and canonical_home canonicalizes the bootstrap path where admission's well_formed compares a non-canonical current_exe (on Linux both are /proc/self/exe, so it agrees; any divergence refuses, i.e. fails closed). No high or critical finding, so no hold.
